miniProject.title: Mutable-priority heap, a derived boundary and a room scheduler
miniProject.brief: Build an indexed heap with `update` and `remove`, checked against a brute-force oracle. Derive one binary-search boundary from its predicate, then solve an unseen tree problem and a two-heap scheduling problem with adversarial tests and a worst-case defense.
steps: Implement an indexed min-heap with `push`, `pop`, `peek`, `update` and `remove` over a position map. State both invariants, heap order and index agreement, with the cost of each operation.

Test it with a Hypothesis state machine against a scanning oracle, checking both invariants after every step. Seed one defect, such as an `update` that only sifts one way, and keep the shrunk history.

Solve LC 1011 Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days with tags hidden. Write the feasibility predicate, prove it monotone and derive the bounds and updates from the loop invariant before running any example.

Solve LC 236 Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree recursively, then add an iterative version with a parent map, since deep paths exceed the default recursion limit. Test both against an ancestor-set oracle on random trees.

Solve LC 2402 Meeting Rooms III with two heaps, freeing rooms by number and busy rooms by end time. Write adversarial tests for delays, ties and back-to-back meetings, and compare against a brute-force simulator on small random inputs.
Write the worst-case notes: the time bound for LC 2402, and why delayed end times overflow fixed-width integers, naming the largest end time the constraints allow.
deliverables: The indexed heap module with invariants, cost notes, the state machine and the seeded-defect history.
The LC 1011 boundary derivation with the monotonicity proof, written before code.
LC 236 and LC 2402 solutions with adversarial and differential tests and worst-case notes.

checks.note: Submit once; the derivation should make the first submission pass.

checks.name: LeetCode 236: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree

rubric.pass: The state machine agrees with the oracle with both invariants checked after every step, and the seeded defect fails with a shrunk history.
rubric.strong: Edge positions such as the root and the last slot are covered, with operation costs checked against the stated bounds.

rubric.pass: The invariant and updates are written before any example runs, and the judge accepts the derived solution.
rubric.strong: A property test checks the answer is the smallest feasible capacity: it holds, and one less fails.

rubric.pass: Both versions agree with the oracle, and the iterative version handles a deep path the recursive one cannot.
rubric.strong: The write-up shows the recursive failure on the deep tree and states the space of each version.

rubric.pass: LC 2402 is accepted, and the simulator agrees on small random inputs with ties and back-to-back meetings.
rubric.strong: The tie rules are stated as heap invariants, with the largest end time derived from the constraints.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone correctness library: the mutable-priority heap. Failure evidence: its seeded defect. The room scheduler is a first scheduler artifact for the milestone.
